source.title: Diversity is All You Need: Learning Skills without a Reward Function

confidence_rationale: Produces a reusable skill library from unsupervised exploration (a capability RND lacks) that accelerates downstream tasks -- but the diversity payoff is largest in high-dim continuous control; on a tiny discrete forage-world few distinct skills exist and RND may already cover them, and DIAYN is the heaviest build of the candidate classes.
failure_signatures: DIAYN's diversity objective and reuse payoff shine in high-dim continuous control; on a small discrete gridworld the number of usefully-distinct skills is small and a novelty bonus may already reach them, so marginal gain over RND may be modest at high build cost.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Learns diverse distinguishable skills with no environment reward by maximizing mutual information between a latent skill code z and visited states (a discriminator predicts z from state), keeping each skill max-entropy; learned skills accelerate downstream task learning and hierarchical control.
mapping.ree_translation: Converts unsupervised exploration into a persistent reusable skill library indexed by z -- a capability neither RND nor REE's transient per-episode curiosity substrate produces -- but at substantial architectural cost.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Payoff (skill reuse across tasks, diversity in large state spaces) is precisely what a single small forage-world may not exercise; on a 5x5-scale substrate the machinery cost likely exceeds the competence it buys unless cross-task reuse is the target.
mapping.source_context: Deep RL, primarily high-dim continuous control (locomotion) + some discrete tasks.

confidence_components.notes: Distinct capability (reusable skills) but heaviest build and weakest fit to a small substrate; deprioritise vs cheaper composable classes.
